definition: KEEPER. neiso-99 arm B, the JOINT arm: it settles BOTH standing NEISO owner escalations in ONE re-solve so they are not confounded (ASSESSMENT-neiso98 §4.1/§4.2). (1) AUDIT ROW O5 — the recipe moves off the ARCHIVED P2 commitment pass onto the production P1 basis; NEISO was the only keeper of six that ran, and was RENDERED FROM, P2, so every published NEISO number sat on a pass CLAUDE.md says no keeper uses. This bundle persists ['P1'] alone. (2) THE STONY BROOK ROUTING DEFECT — _resolve_unit_group's fac_group short-circuit handed a liquid-fuel combustion turbine's outage window to a sibling GAS bin, so plant 6081's two Diesel Oil CTs (83 MW each, 74 windows each) derated a 305.1 MW combined cycle they are not in for 48.7% of the 2024 and 56.0% of the 2025 capacity-year — years in which the CC units 001/002/003 have NO windows of their own at all. Three more NEISO plants were affected (1595 Kendall S6, 568 Bridgeport BHB4, 1588 Mystic MJ-1). Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE]. DETERMINATION CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS, criterion for criterion IDENTICAL to the superseded keeper — 0 FAILs, C3c the sole ledgered caveat, C1 all 12/12 free 8/8, grade scored 8 / target 7 / commercial 0 / ledgered 1 — so NO GATE WAS TRADED for the two corrections, and rule 22 D-5(b)'s worse-determination stop does not fire. THE MOVEMENT IS DECOMPOSED, NOT CONFLATED, against the same-HEAD basis-only control 2026-08-17-neiso-99-basis-p1: the basis leg is a pure re-render (bit-identical to the incumbent's own P1, 0 differing cells every year) worth mean lambda -0.0575 / -0.0110 / -0.0378 and the 2024 annual max $256.93 -> $218.24; the routing leg is worth a further -0.0162 / -0.0133 / -0.1112 $/MWh with the annual maxima unmoved. ONE PREREG EXPECTATION IS REFUTED AND SAID SO: the routing arm's dispatch effect is dominated by KENDALL, not Stony Brook — restoring 6081's availability barely moves its dispatch because that block's heat rate 10.6062 sits above 97.5% of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity (cap-weighted p50 7.340), i.e. it is deep out of merit whether or not it is available, the same fact neiso-83 measured at the same plant. Frontier re-verified on THIS keeper's own sidecars (probe neiso99_declaration_recheck): C3c model tail 0 h > $300/MWh in all three years on the now-sole P1 pass, agreeing with the payload's ordc.hoursGt200.model 0/0/0 vs RT actuals 15/8/20, closest approach $280.85 (short by $19.15); the RCPF co-optimization DORMANT in all 78,840 family-hours at the published statics (1,800/1,200/600 MW) with |dual| max EXACTLY 0.0 — the prior keeper's 1.42e-14 degeneracy noise left with the P2 pass. Prereg PREREG-neiso99-p2basis-routing-2026-08-17.md, pushed before either arm solved.
market_story: CC_REGULAR and CC_CHP: New England's combined-cycle fleet is the marginal energy block in almost every hour, so what the model must get right about it is AVAILABILITY, not offer level. The correction here is availability accounting, not price: two oil-fired peaking turbines at Stony Brook and one at Kendall were having their own maintenance outages charged against the gas blocks they sit next to, so the LP was told a fully-available combined cycle was half gone for most of 2024 and 2025. Real capability came back, and the market story is the ordinary one — an available CHP block runs on its host's steam obligation ahead of merchant CC capacity (CC_CHP +0.053 / +0.064 / +0.022 TWh, mostly Kendall), and a little peaker and oil running is displaced by it (CT_PEAKER -0.001 / -0.004 / -0.019 TWh). CC_REGULAR falls slightly rather than rising, which is the correct and checkable consequence of two facts: the CHP block outranks it, and the block whose availability was restored is Stony Brook, whose 10.61 MMBtu/MWh heat rate puts it above 97.5% of NEISO's CC_REGULAR capacity — it does not run much either way. Prices fall by pennies (-0.016 / -0.013 / -0.111 $/MWh) because cheaper real capability replaced dearer forced running, not because anything was tuned down. oil: the residual 2025 oil energy the lane still carries is unchanged in kind; nothing here forces it.
